page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-8 is an arm64-based virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and it does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The arm64 architecture provides a power-efficient alternative to traditional x86 platforms, offering high resource density for memory-intensive workloads. Because the vCPUs are dedicated, the instance avoids the performance variability associated with shared-core environments. Qualitatively, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides cost-efficient scaling for workloads that require significant memory capacity without requiring a high number of compute cores.

Lacking local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators, the c4a-highmem-8 is not designed for local high-throughput storage operations or GPU-accelerated tasks. It is best suited for memory-bound applications, including medium-sized databases, caching layers, enterprise applications, and memory-intensive web serving or data processing pipelines that run on arm64-compatible software stacks.
